title: Copilot /v1/decisions rejects a personal access token with a plain-text HTTP 400
symptoms: Copilot Decisions (evals) request returns HTTP 400 with a plain-text body containing "Personal Access Tokens are not supported for this endpoint"
A standalone gh-aw evals judge fails as an opaque "Decisions request failed (HTTP 400)" and the run stays green
The same 400 occurs for every model name, including invalid ones, because the token is rejected before model validation
conditions: The request targets the Copilot listener (port 10002) or the Copilot Decisions endpoint at api.githubcopilot.com/v1/decisions
The configured credential is a personal access token in COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN; the reported reproduction used a fine-grained PAT (github_pat_*), and classic PAT acceptance is unverified
The upstream response is a fully captured, decoded 4xx plain-text body; truncated or uninspectable bodies do not receive the reason code
rootCause: The Copilot Decisions endpoint does not accept personal access tokens. AWF forwards the configured credential unchanged and does not exchange a PAT for an OAuth or GitHub App token, so the upstream rejection is returned to the caller. The sidecar classifies the fully captured body as pat_unsupported in logs only. Standalone gh-aw evals run on the host runner outside AWF and cannot be fixed by proxy changes.

probe.expect: Run while containers are kept (--keep-containers). A match shows provider copilot, status 400, and reason_code pat_unsupported on a /v1/decisions request. Compare only the path and status with the failing evals call. Do not print request headers, docker inspect output, or the container environment, and do not issue a Decisions request to test acceptance.

action: Do not switch models, change the Authorization prefix, or route through AWF as a remedy; the rejection precedes model validation. Use an authentication method the endpoint accepts (the Actions job token with copilot-requests: write is the only accepted credential observed, and only for one live request). Keep fine-grained PAT, classic PAT, OAuth, and GitHub App acceptance unverified until a maintainer confirms it. If the evals job runs outside AWF, the classification belongs in gh-aw's client, not the sidecar. Allowlisting api.githubcopilot.com only permits host egress and is not an authentication fix.

references.title: Clarify Copilot Decisions PAT support and rejection diagnostics
docs: clarify Copilot Decisions authentication and egress scope
evals: /v1/decisions rejects fine-grained PATs, and the opaque HTTP 400 hides why
